rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Card Effects 4 Esteemed Guest= 5 Game End Overview Earn more Gold than your opponent OR destroy all their Zeppelins Turn On your turn, take 2 actions which can be the same or different The actions are: Draw, Play, Discard If you draw, take a card into your hand from your personal deck (there is no hand limit) If you play, play a card from your hand to one of your zeppelins as long as that zeppelin does NOT have more cards than any other, then use the effect If you discard, discard the most recent card from one of your Zeppelins and carry out the discard effect Card Effects When you play a card, you carry out the effect based on the quantity of that card in that column If the only copy, do the effect once If second copy, do the effect twice If third copy, do the effect three times then discard all the cards attached to that Zeppelin, discard effects are NOT triggered in this way If you trigger the Maneuvre effect, this does NOT trigger the play effect Esteemed Guest= If you meet their criteria, you immediately take as a free action the corresponding Guest and place it on top of all other treasure collected so far Any treasure below an Esteemed Guest is protected and can't be messed with Game End If the final Zeppelin of a player is destroyed, the other player instantly wins! If a player empties their deck, resolve the rest of their turn, the opponent gets another full turn, then the player with the most accumulated gold wins!

[Rating: 1/10] Every card has blobs of abilities, and they change if you play it or discard it, but you're extremely limited in where you can play... wow this is like the worst of minimalism and maximalism combined. It's so confusing what it's even trying to do. I guess it's a dueling game but you rarely even do that?  My first impression was this reminded me of Sea Salt and Paper. Then I was surprised that designer is listed among the four designers for this. Though it's even worse. Dang, it took four designers to create something this lost and confused?

[Rating: 3/10] Very few decisions to make, actually abandoned the game partway through, despite the presence of a Gentleman T-Rex card. For a 2-player game I expect a lot more strategy and a lot more interest rather than going through the motions like this.

[Rating: 3/10] Interesting twist on the 3 lanes idea with the stacking mechanic and the discard and play abilities.

[Rating: 5/10] Too much randomness for the amount of fiddliness inherit in the different abilities and requirements.
